VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Duties for this position include, but are not limited to: The Registered Nurse (RN)-Ambulatory Surgery Registered Nurse is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to assigned patients and oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the setting.

The nurse will assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization consultation. Demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others. Evaluates practice in an ongoing process, based on best evidence.

Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement. Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes.

Supports colleagues through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care. Shares educational findings, experiences, and ideas with peers. Questions clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care. Participates in activities and strategies to sustain an evidence-based-practice culture.

The Registered Nurse-Ambulatory Surgery Registered Nurse, provides pre-operative/procedural care, including (but not limited to) the nursing assessment of patients, consent, and H&P validations, the starting of intravenous fluids including venipuncture, assisting with peripheral nerve blocks, assuring all lab work and other pre-perative/procedural testing is completed and communicated to team members, confirms surgical sites are prepared and marked, and the administration of medications as ordered.

Provides clear and concise preoperative teaching and reviews discharge instructions to patients and families with written and verbal communication. The Ambulatory RN monitors post-operative patient's level of consciousness after the recovery of anesthesia/sedation. Closely observes signs of side effect of post residual anesthesia medications.

The Ambulatory RN maintains knowledge of current American Society of Peri anesthesia Nurses (ASPAN) standards, VHA Directive and service level standard operating procedures. The Ambulatory RN is responsible for ensuring comprehensive documentation of all phases of care and is timely, complete, and accurate in the electronic health record.

Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards. Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year). Physical Requirements: Physical aspects associated with work required of this assignment are typical for the occupation, see Duties section for essential job duties of the position. May require standing, lifting, carrying, sitting, stooping, bending, pulling, and pushing.

May be required to wear personal protective equipment and undergo annual TB screening or testing as conditions of employment. Work Environment: Work is performed in an office/clinic setting with minimal risks that requires normal safety precautions; the area is adequately lighted, heated, and ventilated.

However, the work environment requires someone with the ability to handle several tasks at once in sometimes stressful situations.

The Specialty Care Outpatient Staff Nurse (RN) is a position located at John Cochran and Jefferson Barracks Campus at VA Saint Louis Health Care System. The Outpatient Staff Nurse is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing and/or supervising direct patient care.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care. Administers medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team.

Core elements of performance include knowledge and active participation in the unit/program level quality improvement process and initiatives as well as customer service programs.

Duties include, but are not limited to: Leads the provision of nursing care to patients with complex care needs utilizing the nursing process in alignment with the ANA Standards of Nursing Practice.

Applies clinical knowledge/judgment to lead staff involvement in planning, decision ­making, and evaluating outcomes within the immediate practice setting. Effectively functions as a leader, with demonstrated outcomes, for the immediate practice setting.

Improves Veteran/patient driven care by resolving experience issues such as coordination of care, timeliness or process issues, common themes of dissatisfaction, or environment of care concerns for the immediate practice setting.

Applies patient, family, and caregiver knowledge, values, and beliefs into care delivery without judgement or discrimination. Serves as an advocate for patients, families, and caregivers, improving outcomes for the immediate practice setting.

Serves as a resource for patients, caregivers, and staff to address and resolve ethical issues in the immediate practice setting. Leads the implementation of high reliability principles and I CARE values to increase consistency of care delivered and improve patient outcomes.

Demonstrates the ability to improve the effectiveness of communications and interactions with others, to inspire their cooperation and confidence to ensure safe and effective outcomes in the current practice setting. Leads teams, contributes to team conferences, and actively collaborates in all phases of patient care planning.

Successfully integrates objectives, opportunities, and resources. Considers alternative courses of action. Respects the opinions, abilities, and contributions of others. Encourages individual growth and development. Effectively sets group goals and keeps self and team informed of the latest trends and developments.

Inspires the cooperation and confidence of others. Demonstrates a high level of expertise. Expands knowledge base and practice evaluation through mentoring, precepting, and/or teaching to improve outcomes in the immediate practice setting. Leads education initiatives to expand knowledge with improved outcomes in the immediate practice setting.

Takes responsibility for personal and professional career goals. Supports the professional growth of others. Participates in the advancement of the profession through mentoring, precepting, and/or teaching.

Physical Requirements: This position requires potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, and sitting. The incumbent may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and may be required to don protective clothing.

The incumbent may occasionally be exposed to patients who are combative secondary to delirium, dementia, or psychiatric disorders. The incumbent must be a mature, flexible, sensible individual capable of working effectively in stressful situations, able to shift priorities based on patient needs.

Must comply with any Employee Health requirements as a condition of employment. This includes but is not limited to moderate carrying/lifting; walking and/or standing for up to six hours at time; and kneeling and repeated bending throughout shift. In the performance of duties,

The Nurse Manager (NM) functions as a clinical expert and is responsible for all aspects of the nursing process when providing or supervising patient care. They assess, plan, implement, and evaluate care based on age-specific needs.

They coordinate care with a focus on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction across the continuum of care. By collaborating with the interdisciplinary team and developing innovative process improvement initiatives, they positively influence care outcomes.

The Nurse Manager will have oversite of ASC/ASU/Pre-anesthesia/PACU/PICC Team/Neuromodulation Clinic/Pain Management Clinic/Ketamine Clinic/and Interventional Radiology. Duties include but not limited to the following: Engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth.

Adheres to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. Equips staff with tools for culturally competent care and promotes a culture of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes.

Cultivates alliances across the care continuum, building trust through active listening, engagement, and emotional intelligence. Contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable, and equitable patient care. Ensures compliance with accreditation and regulatory standards.

Aligns nursing/clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. Promotes an inclusive workplace valuing diversity to achieve the organizations vision and mission. Preferred Experience: Knowledge of ambulatory and inpatient procedural processes. 3-5 years Peri-Operative experience required.

Knowledge of the National Patient Safety Goals as stated by Joint Commission. Superior communication skills to ignite interdisciplinary collaboration. 2-3 years of experience supervising staff. Demonstrated healthcare leadership experience in expanding scope preferred.

Experience in data analysis for evaluation and improvement of performance metrics. Demonstrated success in outcome improvement.

Duties and responsibilities of the COMMUNITY CARE NETWORK (CCN) CARE MANAGER REGISTERED NURSE include, but are not limited to: Community Care Network (CCN) Care Manager, is a registered nurse (RN), who executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex client care within VHA and VA-Community Care program.

RN has the primary responsibility for providing clinical expertise in coordinating Veteran care under the care for Short Term Rehab (30, 60, 90 and up to 100 calendar days) in a Skilled Nursing Facility, in the community for planned and unplanned/emergent episodes of care, and discharge disposition needs.

This includes receipt of initial requests for transfers from community hospitals to skilled nursing facilities under OPTUM. The RN provides close monitoring of continued stay reviews, maintaining nursing standards across service lines, as well as being able to multitask, be flexible and adaptable in the evolving community care environment.

The CCN will collaborate with the Veteran, family, the primary care provider (PCP), the specialty care provider (SCP), the payor, and all other service professionals and paraprofessionals. The CCN will maintain direct, open, and honest communication while adhering to the Veteran's rights of privacy and confidentiality.

The RN will evaluate patient safety and satisfaction, participate in performance improvement projects and monitor data to determine effectiveness of care. The CCN spends substantial time communicating and educating. Therefore, it is vital to possess the skills to communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing.

Responsible for participating within unit based and/or organizational level Shared Governance councils, utilizing clinical expertise, evidence-based practice, and knowledge to assist with finding solutions to problems or issues to improve the quality care provided to our veterans.

The Cardiac Catheterization / Electrophysiology Laboratory / Interventional Radiology (CCL-EP- IR) Nurse II, assumes the following roles and responsibilities: Effectively functions as the team leader, or in other leadership role that guides and directs others who provide patient care.

Performs case management duties to include scheduling, lab review, medication review, and collaboration. Triages phone calls, incoming pre/post-procedural patients, and unit flow. Organizes and coordinates staff and resources to identify and address unit problems, issues, and needs to improve existing processes.

Initiates collaborating with other disciplines/departments to achieve desired patient outcomes. Coordinates unit flow to maintain efficiency. Nous proposons une offre complète de soins en cabinet, de soins à domicile, de centres de prélèvement, de transport médical ainsi que des prestations d’aide pratique, de veilles et de présences à domicile.

Afin de renforcer notre équipe de liaison, nous recherchons un·e :
Infirmier·ère polyvalent·e (60 à 80 %)

En tant qu’infirmier·ère polyvalent·e, vous assurez une prise en charge globale et de qualité des patients, en collaboration étroite avec les responsables et le service de coordination, les référents des soins, les médecins, les familles et les différents partenaires du réseau de santé.
Votre activité combine soins infirmiers, coordination, prélèvements biologiques, suivi des patients et tâches médico-administratives, dans une approche centrée sur les besoins de chaque patient.
Vos principales responsabilités
1. Soins et prise en charge des patients
Dispenser des soins infirmiers ambulatoires et à domicile, adaptés à l’état de santé et à la complexité des situations.
Assurer le suivi global des patients et l’actualisation des dossiers, plans de traitement et plans de soins.
Veiller à la bonne application des prescriptions médicales.
Réagir de manière appropriée à l’évolution de l’état de santé des patients.
Garantir la continuité, la sécurité et la qualité de la prise en charge.
2. Prélèvements biologiques et soins techniques
Réaliser les prélèvements biologiques (sang, urines et autres échantillons) selon les prescriptions médicales.
Préparer le patient et le matériel nécessaire aux prélèvements.
Respecter strictement les règles d’hygiène, d’asepsie et de sécurité.
Assurer l’identification, l’étiquetage, la traçabilité et l’acheminement des prélèvements vers les laboratoires.
Garantir le double contrôle lors de toute modification de traitement, notamment pour les traitements IV.
3. Coordination et liaison
Coordonner la prise en charge avec les médecins traitants, les patients, les familles et les différents professionnels de santé.
Assurer la liaison avec les établissements de soins et les partenaires externes.
Préparer et coordonner les admissions, consultations, hospitalisations et retours à domicile.
Assurer une transmission complète et fluide des informations entre les différents intervenants.
Participer au suivi des prescriptions OPAS et aux échanges avec les assureurs.
Assurer un suivi régulier avec les médecins et partenaires impliqués dans la prise en charge.
4. Planification et organisation
Organiser et planifier les prestations, rendez-vous et interventions.
Gérer les priorités en fonction des besoins des patients et des directives institutionnelles.
Veiller au respect des délais de prise en charge et de réponse aux demandes.
Participer à l’organisation et à la répartition des activités au sein de l’équipe.

s.h: We have an opening for a
s.t:
RN - Clinical Field Reviewer (Remote in Montana)
The RN Clinical Field Reviewer is a remote position that requires in-home nursing assessments which require the successful candidate to reside in one of the following Montana counties: Gallatin, Park, Sweetgrass, Stillwater, Carbon, or Yellowstone.
We are a team of Registered Nurses working remotely across the state of Montana completing in-home nursing assessments of eligible members living in the areas where we live for the Medicaid CFCS/PCS (Community First Choice Services/Personal Care Services) program.

We conduct person-centered in-home nursing assessments focused on a member’s functional abilities and their needs for ADL and IADL assistance initially, annually, and as needed if a change in condition occurs for members of all ages.

We have a shared goal of keeping members independent in their homes with the assistance of paid caregivers and informal support. We work closely with provider agencies across the state to ensure that services are being delivered to members as authorized following policies set forth by the State of Montana DPHHS.

We empower members to become participants in their care through active listening and planning with their input, provide care coordination, practice cultural humility with each client, and utilize evidence-based practice as a foundation for our interventions.
The ideal candidate should have experience with home visits and passion for helping others while working independently in the field. You set your own schedule and are responsible for meeting your timelines.
This position requires travel by personal car to locations throughout Gallatin, Park, Sweetgrass, Stillwater, Carbon, and Yellowstone County in Montana to complete in-home assessments, reliable home internet, and a current Montana Registered Nursing (RN) license.

The ideal candidate should have experience with home visits and passion for helping others while working independently in the field. Experience with home health, hospice, or long-term care is preferred. The position is full-time, flexible schedule, 30-40 hours per week.

The successful candidate will be responsible to set their own schedule and meet all deadlines. Mountain Pacific does reimburse mileage at the current federal rate.

Die Diagnose ist gestellt – und dann? Für viele Erwachsene mit ADHS beginnt genau hier die Arbeit, die ihren Alltag wirklich verändert: Struktur finden, mit dem Arbeitgeber sprechen, Ansprüche klären, dranbleiben. Diesen Teil der Versorgung bauen wir neu auf, und du gestaltest ihn mit.
klaroADHS ist ein spezialisiertes ambulantes Angebot für die Abklärung und Behandlung von ADHS bei Erwachsenen, mit Standorten in Zürich und Biel und ergänzender Videosprechstunde. Trägerin ist die 1050medical GmbH. Rund 20 Mitarbeitende arbeiten bei uns interprofessionell zusammen: Fachärztinnen und Fachärzte für Psychiatrie und Psychotherapie, Assistenzärztinnen und \-ärzte, Psycholog:innen und ein Administrationsteam.
Was dich erwartet
* Du führst begleitende Einzelgespräche nach der Diagnosestellung – vor Ort und per Videosprechstunde
* Du leistest Psychoedukation zu ADHS im Erwachsenenalter, zunächst im Einzelsetting, später auch in Gruppen
* Du unterstützt bei Alltagsstruktur, Arbeitssituation und Selbstmanagement
* Du berätst zu Arbeit, Sozialversicherungen und Nachteilsausgleich und führst Angehörigen\- und Arbeitgebergespräche
* Du koordinierst mit weiterbehandelnden Fachpersonen und externen Fachstellen
* Du dokumentierst den Verlauf sorgfältig
* Du bringst dein Wissen in Fallbesprechungen ein und arbeitest unter der fachlichen Verantwortung unserer Fachärztinnen und Fachärzte
Was du mitbringst
* Diplom als Pflegefachperson HF/FH mit Fachrichtung Psychiatrie, Bachelor in Sozialer Arbeit FH oder ein gleichwertiger Abschluss
* Berufserfahrung im psychiatrischen Umfeld
* Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (mind. C1\); für den Standort Biel zusätzlich gute Französischkenntnisse
* Regelmässige Präsenz an einem der beiden Standorte möglich
* Wertschätzende, ressourcenorientierte Haltung
* Freude daran, einen Bereich von Grund auf mitzuentwickeln statt in fertige Strukturen einzusteigen
Von Vorteil, aber keine Bedingung: ambulante Erfahrung, Kenntnisse im Sozialversicherungsrecht, eine Zusatzqualifikation im Bereich ADHS oder Coaching.
Was wir dir bieten
* Ein Bereich, den du prägst: Du baust die Begleitung nach der Diagnosestellung mit auf – Konzept, Ablauf und Gruppenangebot entstehen mit dir
* Fachlich begleitet: regelmässige Fallbesprechungen und Supervision durch unsere Fachärztinnen und Fachärzte
* Wissen, das weiterbringt: Wir beteiligen uns an deiner Weiterbildung, mit Beitrag und Weiterbildungstagen
* Planbar: Montag bis Freitag, keine Wochenend\-, Nacht\- und Pikettdienste
* Flexibel: Pensum und Aufteilung zwischen Präsenz und Videosprechstunde legen wir gemeinsam fest
* Erholung: 5 Wochen Ferien, ab 50 Jahren 6 Wochen
* Zentral: Arbeitsort in Zürich oder Biel, gut mit dem ÖV erreichbar
Deine Bewerbung
Schick uns Lebenslauf, Diplome und ein paar Sätze dazu, warum dich dieses Feld interessiert. Schreib uns bitte auch, welcher Standort für dich infrage kommt. Wir melden uns innerhalb einer Woche.
